function.name: calculate_investment_value
function.description: Calculate the future value of an investment given the principal, interest rate and term. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

principal.description: The initial amount of the investment. This is a float type value.

interest_rate.description: The annual interest rate in percentage. Enter as a decimal (for 5%, enter 0.05). This is a float type value.

term.description: The term of the investment in years.

compounding.description: The number of times that interest is compounded per year. Default is 1 (annually).

message.content:
Here’s a quick mix of classic, cult‑favorite, and recent horror films that have kept audiences on the edge of their seats:

| # | Title | Year | Why It’s Worth Watching |
|---|-------|------|------------------------|
| 1 | **Psycho** | 1960 | Hitchcock’s masterclass in suspense and the iconic shower scene. |
| 2 | **The Shining** | 1980 | A chilling psychological descent set in an isolated hotel. |
| 3 | **The Exorcist** | 1973 | One of the most unsettling supernatural tales ever made. |
| 4 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | A modern psychological horror that redefines dread. |
| 5 | **Get Out** | 2017 | A smart blend of social commentary and genuine scares. |
| 6 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | Silence is survival—thrilling, tense, and emotionally resonant. |
| 7 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | Daylight horror that turns a festival into a nightmare. |
| 8 | **It Follows** | 2014 | A fresh take on the “invisible stalker” trope. |
| 9 | **The Conjuring** | 2013 | A modern supernatural franchise grounded in real‑life investigations. |
|10 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | A psychological horror that doubles as a powerful mother‑daughter story. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—whether you like psychological dread, supernatural chills, or slasher thrills!
